notApplicable.hdt045: HDT is a rigid-bar test. ISO 75 ends at 0.2 % outer-fibre strain, which a bar reaches once its modulus falls to about 225 MPa, so an elastomer has no meaningful HDT and makers list it as N/A. A value an elastomer's sheet publishes is shown and never decides. Sintering filaments are left out too: the finished part is the sintered metal or ceramic.

items.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
items.text: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.
items.conditions: Lengthy exposure
items.note: Columns: Elastollan standard ester grades (e.g. 500, 800), Elastollan C 85 A, Elastollan ether grades (e.g. 1100); each at 23 °C and 60 °C, resistance expressed as hours, days, weeks, months or years. Harder products swell less and resist better. A filament's base (ester or ether) is usually not published.

items.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyether-based TPU)
items.text: Because of its chemical structure, polyether-based Elastollan is much more resistant to hydrolytic degradation (Figures 41 and 42 compare Elastollan 1185 A ether grade with C 85 A ester grade between 50 and 100 °C).
